candidate: B — Temporal (live dev server, temporalio@1.9.3 SDK, server 1.31.2 via CLI 1.8.2, SQLite)
workload: 4-phase DAG ro1->ro2->writer->verifier (mirrors DE-1); activities append to an append-only side-effect marker log + writer artifact; real SIGKILL of the worker process
method: per-scenario task queue + per-scenario side-effect log (hermetic; no cross-run contamination); worker killed with SIGKILL; activity heartbeat 150ms, heartbeatTimeout 2s, startToClose 60s, retry max 10
serverHistoryVerified: for every scenario the Temporal server history records exactly ONE ActivityTask per phase (no server-side duplication); side-effect log counts are the app-observable executions

results.name: crash during node (kill mid-p_ro1)
results.detail: worker SIGKILLed mid-activity -> activity task re-dispatched after heartbeat timeout (2s) -> WHOLE activity re-executed from scratch (attempt 2) -> workflow completed. Recovery latency includes the full 4s activity re-run + ~2s heartbeat timeout + re-dispatch. No lost completed result, no duplicate.

results.name: result persisted / successor not scheduled (kill after p_ro1)
results.detail: worker killed immediately after p_ro1 completion: p_ro1 result was PERSISTED in history (ro1Started=1, NOT re-executed) and the successor was re-dispatched. The kill raced successor scheduling (worker processed the next task within the ~50ms poll lag), so no standalone recovery gap was observable; the persistence property (no duplicate ro1) held.

results.name: writer side-effect boundary (RAW naive, kill after mutation)
results.detail: KEY FINDING: writer activity committed its side effect (artifact + mutation marker), then the worker was SIGKILLed before the activity completed. At-least-once semantics re-executed the WHOLE activity (attempt 2) and the mutation was applied AGAIN -> 1 duplicate writer mutation. Temporal does NOT protect the writer side-effect boundary by default; the app must implement idempotency.

results.name: writer side-effect boundary (idempotent commit-token, kill after mutation)
results.detail: same kill, but the writer uses a commit-token pattern (dedupe key written atomically with the mutation, checked on activity start). Retry detected the committed token and skipped the mutation -> exactly-once writer side effect under the same failure. The idempotency pattern works but is APP-LEVEL code, not a framework guarantee.

results.name: duplicate recovery (same workflowId restart)
results.detail: defaultReuse=NEW_EXECUTION_ALLOWED rejectDuplicate=NEW_EXECUTION_ALLOWED after COMPLETED; REJECT_DUPLICATE vs RUNNING -> WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_ALREADY_STARTED. FINDING: Temporal's workflowId reuse policy does NOT provide an automatic exactly-once invocation guard after completion — the default policy allows a new execution with the same workflowId, and REJECT_DUPLICATE only rejects while the workflow is RUNNING (not after COMPLETED). An app needing 'duplicate recovery invocation returns the existing result with zero re-execution' (STACK_A T11 behavior) must implement explicit idempotency (e.g., idempotency key at start + AlreadyStarted handling).

results.name: corrupt state / checkpoint equivalent (corrupt SQLite history copy)
results.detail: SQLite integrity_check on the corrupted copy DETECTED the corruption (malformed disk image (11), multiple btree errors). A second dev server started on the corrupted db and served a describe() for a known workflow (status=TERMINATED, a valid state — no wrong data returned). FINDING: corruption is detected by SQLite integrity_check but the Temporal server does NOT proactively validate on startup — it fails lazily when corrupted pages are accessed. No silent wrong data was observed; the detection is deferred vs STACK_A which rejects a tampered checkpoint at resume time (fail-closed at the detection point).

safetyHardGates.lostCompletedResult: 0 across all scenarios (server history verified: each phase completed exactly once server-side)
safetyHardGates.duplicateWriterMutation: 1 in S3 (RAW at-least-once re-execution); 0 in S4 (idempotent pattern); 0 in all others
safetyHardGates.authorityEscalation: not applicable (no authority model in Temporal harness; framework does not manage AutoLoop authority)

summary: Temporal (live) recovers automatically from worker crashes via re-dispatch + deterministic replay, with zero lost completed results. Its at-least-once activity semantics re-execute ENTIRE activities from scratch after a mid-activity kill (no activity-level checkpointing), which duplicates committed side effects unless the app implements idempotency (S3 vs S4). WorkflowId reuse does not give an automatic exactly-once invocation guard after completion (S5). Corrupt state is detected by SQLite but validated lazily, not proactively (S6).
